course.title: Barbing
course.tagline: Cut clean fades, shape-ups and styles with clippers and skill, and finish your first paying client.

days.title: Welcome to Barbing
days.goal: By the end of today you can explain and practise: Your kit is clippers, trimmers, guards 0 to 8, a comb, scissors, a cape and a spray bottle.

video.title: How to Fade Hair the Easy Way

steps: Get your tools ready: clipper with guards, trimmer and foil shaver.
Watch the video. It explains the main point in simple steps: A clipper guard number equals one-eighth of an inch of hair left behind.
Your kit is clippers, trimmers, guards 0 to 8, a comb, scissors, a cape and a spray bottle. Go slowly. Practise on a model or a practice head.
Do the same move three times. Check your work in a mirror or a photo after each try.
Write down what went well, what was hard, and one thing to do better tomorrow.
days.task: Practise welcome to barbing on a model or a practice head. Your kit is clippers, trimmers, guards 0 to 8, a comb, scissors, a cape and a spray bottle. Take a photo of your work.
days.challenge: Do welcome to barbing two times today. Make the second try neater than the first.

quiz.q: What does a clipper guard number tell you?
options: How much hair the guard leaves behind
How fast the clipper cuts
How sharp the blade is
How long the haircut will take
quiz.explain: A higher guard number leaves more hair behind. A number 1 guard leaves about one-eighth of an inch.

quiz.q: Which tool do you need most for a fade?
options: Clipper with guards
Round brush
Hair dryer
Flat iron
quiz.explain: A clipper with guards is the main tool for fading. You change guards to blend the hair from short to long.

quiz.q: What should you always do between clients?
options: Disinfect your clippers
Use a hot iron on wet hair
Skip cleaning to save time
Use the same cape without shaking it out
quiz.explain: Always disinfect your clippers between clients. Clean tools keep every client safe.

days.title: Know Your Tools
days.goal: By the end of today you can explain and practise: Learn each clipper, trimmer, foil shaver, comb and shear, and what job each one does.

video.title: How to Fade Hair for Beginners

steps: Get your tools ready: clipper with guards, trimmer and foil shaver.
Watch the video. It explains the main point in simple steps: A foil shaver cuts hair closest to the skin for a clean skin finish.
Learn each clipper, trimmer, foil shaver, comb and shear, and what job each one does. Go slowly. Practise on a model or a practice head.
Do the same move three times. Check your work in a mirror or a photo after each try.
Write down what went well, what was hard, and one thing to do better tomorrow.
days.task: Practise know your tools on a model or a practice head. Learn each clipper, trimmer, foil shaver, comb and shear, and what job each one does. Take a photo of your work.
days.challenge: Do know your tools two times today. Make the second try neater than the first.

quiz.q: What is the key point of today's lesson on know your tools?
options: The best result comes from skipping the preparation step.
You never need to check your work until the very end.
A foil shaver cuts hair closest to the skin for a clean skin finish.
Using dirty tools gives the same result as clean ones.
quiz.explain: A foil shaver cuts hair closest to the skin for a clean skin finish.

quiz.q: Which tool is most essential for know your tools?
options: round brush
hair dryer
flat iron
trimmer
quiz.explain: The trimmer is the essential tool for this work.

quiz.q: What should you always do when working on know your tools?
options: never cut broken skin
always use heat protectant before hot tools
never use a hot tool on soaking wet hair
test the iron temperature on a strand first
quiz.explain: Never cut broken skin.
